verdict.line: You lose if Volibear's Q (Thundering Smash) stun connects first and chains into W (Frenzied Maul) and autos before level 6; you win if you poke him down with Infernal Chains and Umbral Dash trades while his Q and E are both on cooldown.

brief.thesis: Volibear's whole kit except E (Sky Splitter, 1200 range, 16s cooldown) requires him to already be standing on you — Q (Thundering Smash) is a 300-range stun and W (Frenzied Maul) is a 325-range poke on a 5s cooldown. Aatrox's W (Infernal Chains, 825 range) does not have that restriction, so you decide when the fight starts. Umbral Dash's passive heal on damaging champions means every trade you initiate from range pays you back; the 50.3% head-to-head win rate over 2,390 games reflects a lane that's close only because Volibear punishes you hard if you let him close the gap first.

brief.thesis: This matchup is a race between two self-sustaining melee kits, and the data confirms it's coin-flip close at 50.9% over 1324 games. Yorick's Q (Last Rites) heals him on landed empowered autos, which is exactly why OP.GG warns against prolonged melee combat — every extra second of brawling is a heal tick for him. Aatrox's actual edge is burst: W (Infernal Chains) forces a reposition into range-825 damage, and if he doesn't clear the zone he's dragged in and hit again, which is the setup for a short violent trade rather than a long one. Before level 6, Yorick has no Maiden to extend fights or split-push with, which is where Aatrox's solo-kill advantage actually lives.

yourWindow.when: His E and R are both on cooldown

Whoever tracks the other's cooldowns and terrain better wins the lane, not raw stats.

There is no inherent lane-advantage to lean on here — the matchup is decided by execution, not champion identity.

theirWindow.when: Sett's Grit is full, W off cooldown
theirWindow.what: Haymaker expends all stored Grit for a shield and punches a center that deals true damage with physical damage on the sides. Do not stand in the middle of his attack-back animation when his Grit bar is topped off — back off a step or force the trade from range with Q instead.

yourWindow.when: Sett's E (Facebreaker) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Facebreaker only stuns if you're caught on opposite sides of him (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown); with it down he has no hard CC besides R. Commit E (Apprehend) to hook him in and stack Hemorrhage freely.

playing.detail: Decimate deals more damage to enemies struck by the blade than the handle, so land it at max range rather than point-blank. This also keeps you off-center from Sett's W (Haymaker) punch zone.

playing.title: Track Sett's Grit bar before trading
playing.detail: Haymaker's damage and shield scale off stored Grit from damage he's taken. If his Grit looks empty, he has no shield to trade through — this is when your auto/Q poke hits hardest relative to his retaliation.

playing.title: Stay on one side of Sett
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if you're caught on opposite sides of him; if you're always on the same side as his jungle or minions, it only slows you, not stuns.

playing.title: Hook with E before all-inning
playing.detail: Apprehend pulls him to you and passively shreds a percentage of his Armor — use it to start the fight on your terms rather than trading into his engage.

playing.title: Hold R until stacks are high
playing.detail: Noxian Guillotine deals true damage that scales per stack of Hemorrhage on the target; don't throw it at one or two stacks when it can finish a near-five-stack target instead.

playing.title: Punish his R cooldown
playing.detail: The Show Stopper is on a 120/100/80/80/80s cooldown. After he uses it, whether it lands or not, he has no grab or stun available — look to force fights in that window.

brief.thesis: Shen's only answers to a committed Darius all-in are Feint's self-shield (9/8/7/6/5s cd) and Shadow Dash's taunt (16/14/12/10/8s cd), and both are single-use cooldowns with real downtime. Darius stacks Hemorrhage faster than Shen can out-sustain it with Vorpal Blade's life tap, and once those two cooldowns are spent Shen has no tool left to stop a Noxian Guillotine finish. That structural gap is why Darius sits at 54.4% over 114 games here against a 49.5% baseline.

playing.title: Hold W through his engage

brief.thesis: K'Sante's W (Path Maker) charge-up and stacking Q (Ntofo Strikes) let him force short, violent trades before Irelia has a reliable answer, which is why he holds both lane and solo-kill advantage pre-6. Irelia's kit doesn't have a hard counter to that burst window, it has a longer scaling curve — Q (Bladesurge) resets and item power catch up by the early-to-mid game, which is why the measured matchup settles back to roughly even.

theirWindow.what: At 2 stacks his next Q fires a shockwave that pulls you in, which chains straight into his W (Path Maker) knockback-stun. Don't stand in his short-line Q range back-to-back, and if you're already caught, charge W (Defiant Dance) immediately since it reduces the physical damage you take while charging and blunts that combo.

yourWindow.when: His W and E are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: W (Path Maker, 14-10s CD) is his only stun/knockback and E (Footwork, 10-8s CD) is his only shield/dash — with neither up he has no disengage and no mitigation. Land E (Flawless Duet) for the stun and Mark, then Q (Bladesurge) into him; the Mark refreshes Q's cooldown so you can dash a second time to finish.

verdict.line: You lose if Kled lands Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) into a double Jousting dash before level 6; you win if you survive to Blade of the Ruined King and punish him the moment Skaarl dismounts.

brief.thesis: Kled's entire kit is built around an early burst all-in — hook with Q (Bear Trap on a Rope), then dash in and back out with E (Jousting) — that outpaces Irelia before she has passive stacks or items, which is why Kled holds both the lane edge and the solo-kill edge at a 44.2% Irelia win rate over 77 games. That burst collapses the instant Skaarl's mount health empties, because Kled's abilities change and he deals less damage to champions while dismounted — that is the one moment your stacked Ionian Fervor and Q (Bladesurge) resets actually win the fight.

yourWindow.what: Dismounted Kled deals less damage to champions and his Q becomes the knockback Pocket Pistol. Commit everything now — Bladesurge resets off a Marked target so you can double-tap Q through the kill window.

verdict.line: You lose if you stand and auto-trade into a charged Granite Shield or a Brutal Strikes buff; you win if you poke the shield down first and then stun-engage the moment his E (Ground Slam) is on cooldown.

brief.thesis: Malphite's passive, Granite Shield, absorbs a chunk of whatever burst hits it first and only recharges if he hasn't been hit recently — so Irelia's normal Q (Bladesurge) dash-in gets partially eaten unless the shield is already down from prior chip damage. Layer on Ground Slam, a 400-range shockwave on a 7s cooldown that reduces attack speed, and standing in extended auto trades is a losing pattern. The 45.2% win rate over 2,245 games reflects players trading like it's a normal duel instead of a shield-bait-then-burst matchup.

brief.thesis: Mordekaiser's Darkness Rise passive only triggers after he lands three attacks or spells on you, and Indestructible (W) is what lets him heal through long fights — so this matchup is entirely about trade length. Irelia's kit is built for short trades: E (Flawless Duet) stuns and Marks, Q (Bladesurge) refreshes instantly off a Marked or killed target, and that dash can reset onto a minion just as easily as a champion to disengage. Stay in his face past the third hit and you lose the fight on his terms; dash in, stun, hit, and leave, and you win it on yours.

verdict.line: You lose if Volibear lands Q's stun and chains into a healing W before your Counter Strike is off cooldown; you win almost every extended trade once Counter Strike and the free-cooldown Relentless Assault are both online.

brief.thesis: Volibear's early kit is built around short-cooldown tools — a 5-second Frenzied Maul and a sub-12-second Thundering Smash — that let him chain a stun into sustain-healing autos faster than Jax can answer with an 18-second rank-1 Counter Strike. But Jax's Relentless Assault has zero cooldown, so once both ultimates are up, every extended trade turns into an auto-attack race that rewards the attack-speed-stacker over the healer. That structural flip from short trades to long ones is why Jax holds both the lane and solo-kill edge (53.4% over 234 games) despite losing some early skirmishes.

yourWindow.when: the instant Volibear commits his Q dash
yourWindow.what: Pop Counter Strike as he closes in — it dodges the basic attack his Q needs to land the stun, so you take nothing from the engage and stun him back instead. Follow with an Empowered Leap Strike and let Relentless Assault's stacking attack speed carry the rest of the fight.

verdict.line: You lose if Aatrox closes to melee and chains Deathbringer Stance procs with Umbral Dash heals in extended trades; you win if you live in Cannon stance, poke with Shock Blast (Q) from range 600, and buy Executioner's Calling to shut his sustain down.

brief.thesis: Aatrox stacks two independent sustain sources — the periodic empowered auto-heal from his passive Deathbringer Stance, and the on-hit champion heal from Umbral Dash (E) — onto a dash-and-pull package (Umbral Dash's dash, Infernal Chains' 825-range drag) that lets him force exactly the extended melee trade Jayce's base kit loses. Jayce's only path to the 48.1% head-to-head win rate over 4692 games is denying that trade entirely: stay in Cannon stance and fire Shock Blast (Q) from outside his reach instead of ever matching him in Hammer stance.

theirWindow.when: When Umbral Dash (E) is up
theirWindow.what: He can dash onto you and his passive Deathbringer Stance heals him off the next basic attack while Umbral Dash itself heals him on the hit. Do not melee trade here — hold Cannon stance and kite, or knock him back the instant he lands.

yourWindow.when: When his Q and E are both down
yourWindow.what: With Umbral Dash (E) and his Darkin Blade (Q) swings on cooldown he has no way to close the gap or punish a miss. Swap to Cannon stance and fire Shock Blast (Q) freely.

boots.why: 50% win rate over 2084 games; the cooldown reduction lets Jayce swap Cannon/Hammer stance with R (cooldown 6s) and recast Shock Blast (Q) more often to keep poke tempo up.

runes.keystoneWhy: The movespeed burst after sustained ability use lets Jayce kite out of Infernal Chains (W, range 825) and Umbral Dash (E) instead of getting pinned into the melee trade Aatrox wants.

summoners.why: Most-run and highest-winrate combo (48.9% win rate, 62.5% pick); Ignite's Grievous Wounds directly undercuts Deathbringer Stance's heal and Umbral Dash's on-hit healing, and Flash is your main way to dodge a landed Infernal Chains (W) pull.

playing.title: Live in Cannon stance
playing.detail: Poke with Shock Blast (Q, cooldown 16/14/12/10/8s, range 600) whenever Umbral Dash (E) and Infernal Chains (W) are down. Swapping to Hammer stance to melee trade is exactly where his Deathbringer Stance heal and Umbral Dash sustain punish you.

playing.title: Respect the 825-range chain
playing.detail: Infernal Chains (W, cooldown 20/18/16/14/12s, range 825) outranges your 600-range Q leap. Track its cooldown and don't walk up near minimum distance, or you'll be dragged to the impact center and take the damage twice.

playing.title: Punish his dash with a knockback
playing.detail: Umbral Dash (E, cooldown 9/8/7/6/5s) heals Aatrox on the hit he lands. The instant he dashes onto you, swap to Hammer stance and knock him back with E (Thundering Blow, range 240) to break off the trade.

playing.title: Buy into his sustain
playing.detail: Once he's landing Deathbringer Stance autos and healing off Umbral Dash, pick up Executioner's Calling (per OP.GG data) for Grievous Wounds — it blunts both heal sources at once.

playing.title: Gate your Shock Blast
playing.detail: Drop the Cannon-stance Acceleration Gate (E) and fire Shock Blast (Q) through it for increased missile speed, range, and damage — this lands full pokes from outside his Darkin Blade swing range.

playing.title: Track his ultimate timer
playing.detail: World Ender (R, cooldown 120/100/80/80/80s) extends on any takedown and buffs his AD, healing, and move speed. If he's picked up a kill anywhere on the map recently, assume it's back up and play trades tighter.

brief.thesis: This is a cooldown-reading lane, not a stat-check: Jayce's Cannon-stance Shock Blast (Q) poke only works when Camille's Hookshot (E, 16/15/14/13/12s) is on cooldown, and Camille's all-in only works if she lands Tactical Sweep (W) or Hookshot clean. 127,458 games put Jayce at 47.7% in this role and 2,536 head-to-head games put this specific pairing at 45.6%, which OP.GG itself calls an even lane with an even solo-kill rate — the numbers say skill and cooldown tracking decide it, not champion identity.

theirWindow.when: Her E (Hookshot) is up near a wall
theirWindow.what: She can pull to the wall, leap off, and knock up on landing, then chain Precision Protocol (Q) and a point-blank Tactical Sweep (W) for a full trade. Don't stand in range of a wall she can hook to, and if she commits the dash anyway, hold Thundering Blow (E) to knock her back out of her follow-up window.

yourWindow.when: Her E (Hookshot) is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Swap to Cannon stance and poke freely with Shock Blast (Q), ideally through an Acceleration Gate (E) for the extra missile speed, range, and damage — she has no gap closer to punish the poke.

playing.title: Poke only when her E is down
playing.detail: Track Hookshot's (E) 16-12s cooldown by range and track her last cast. Swap to Cannon stance and fire Shock Blast (Q) through an Acceleration Gate (E) in that window for free damage.

playing.title: Respect her W before level 3
playing.detail: Tactical Sweep (W) is a cone after a delay that slows and heals on the outer half — getting clipped by it pre-level-3 is the single biggest reason this lane tips to her.

playing.title: Knock her back mid-dash
playing.detail: When she commits Hookshot (E) to leap off a wall at you, hold Thundering Blow (E) to knock her away before she can follow up with an empowered Precision Protocol (Q) auto.

playing.title: Don't stand near hookable walls
playing.detail: Hookshot (E) has 800 range but needs a wall behind you — holding mid-lane space instead of the river/tri-brush denies her the engage entirely.

playing.title: Bank mana until Tear is up
playing.detail: Lightning Field's (W) passive restores mana per strike in Hammer stance, but don't dump your bar on poke before Tear of the Goddess comes online or you'll have nothing for the all-in.

playing.title: Shred her shield once you're ahead
playing.detail: Adaptive Defenses gives her a shield off your own autos — once you're building Serpent's Fang, your poke stops feeding her sustain.

playing.title: Swap stances for the first-hit bonus
playing.detail: R's first attack after transforming either reduces armor/MR (Cannon) or adds magic damage (Hammer) — time the swap to land right as she commits to a trade.

verdict.line: You lose when you eat a Rupture into a level-6 Feast all-in; you win nearly every poke war once your core items land.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's only real poke, Rupture, actually outranges your Shock Blast (950 vs 600) and is on a 9s cooldown, so this lane is a patience check: bait the Q, punish the long whiff window, and never let him land it into a Feral Scream or a level-6 Feast. The numbers back that up — 49.3% Jayce win rate over 205 games, with lane and solo-kill edge on your side once you play it right.

theirWindow.when: Right after Rupture lands on you
theirWindow.what: He'll walk in to stack Vorpal Spikes autos, and from level 6 on a low-HP target he can follow with Feast for a near-instant kill. Disengage immediately instead of trading through the knock-up.

yourWindow.when: Right after Cho'Gath whiffs Rupture
yourWindow.what: He has no gap-close and Rupture is down for 9s — flip to Cannon Stance and punish with Shock Blast or Hyper Charge-empowered autos before he can reset to max range.

playing.detail: Hold max range in Cannon Stance so his Q (Rupture, 950 range, 9s cooldown) has to be thrown speculatively. The instant it misses, flip stance and punish with Shock Blast or empowered autos before it's back up.

playing.title: Never auto-trade into fresh spikes
playing.detail: E (Vorpal Spikes) procs on every one of his autos at point-blank range with a 0.5s cooldown — walking into melee to trade autos loses to this every time, especially pre-6.

playing.title: Respect Feral Scream from level 4 on
playing.detail: W (Feral Scream) is a 300-range cone that silences. Getting tagged mid-combo cancels your stance-swap rotation outright, so stay past 300 range whenever its 13s cooldown is up.

playing.title: Play around Feast at level 6
playing.detail: R (Feast) deals high true damage at 175 range and grows him on a kill (max 6 stacks). Don't sit below roughly 30% HP inside his melee range once he hits 6.

playing.title: Spike hard after Tear into Muramana
playing.detail: Once Muramana is online your Shock Blast poke scales sharply and Youmuu's active lets you disengage after every bait — this is your best all-in window of the game (levels 9-13).

playing.title: Clear waves from range, not melee
playing.detail: Use Cannon Stance Shock Blast to shove and clear from max range instead of auto-trading. This denies his Vorpal Spikes stacks and the health/mana he recovers from Carnivore on kills.

playing.title: Pick Mercury's Treads over Lucidity here
playing.detail: Tenacity shortens both Feral Scream's silence and Rupture's slow, which breaks the exact chain he needs to land a kill — take this whenever he's landing CC combos, not just for raw stats.

theirWindow.when: Riposte is up and she's in range
theirWindow.what: She can parry and negate your next auto or Thundering Blow for free magic damage back. Don't throw E (Thundering Blow) or walk up for a poke auto while her W is clearly available — bait it out with a minion or your Shock Blast orb instead.

yourWindow.when: Her Riposte is on cooldown
yourWindow.what: This is your window to full-combo: swap to Hammer, land Thundering Blow (E) for the knockback, then follow with autos or swap back to Cannon for Shock Blast poke. She has no answer to your damage while W is down.

verdict.line: You lose if you stand in melee range past level 2 and eat a Fury-fueled stun chain; you win if you abuse ranged Cannon Stance poke before he hits his stride.

brief.thesis: Renekton's Fury bar is the whole matchup: below 50 Fury his W (Ruthless Predator) is a two-hit stun with moderate damage, but above 50 it becomes a three-hit stun that strips shields and hits for high damage, so the fight you can safely take at 40 Fury is not the fight you can take at 60. Jayce's job is to poke from range in Cannon Stance, deny him easy Fury generation from autos, and only let Hammer Stance E (Thundering Blow) or Q (To the Skies!) commit when his Fury is low or his E (Slice and Dice) is down.

theirWindow.when: Fury above 50 and E up
theirWindow.what: He can dash in, land an empowered three-hit W stun that shreds shields, and follow with a big Q heal. Do not trade in melee here; disengage with Q Cannon Stance or kite with E Acceleration Gate.

yourWindow.when: His E (Slice and Dice) on cooldown (16/14.5/13/11.5/10s)
yourWindow.what: He has no gap close, so sit at max range in Cannon Stance and fire Q (Shock Blast) and auto with W (Hyper Charge) attack speed active. This is your highest-value poke window all lane.

verdict.line: You lose if you melee-trade into Riven's Q-W stun combo; you win if you stay in Cannon stance and poke her down before she ever gets to use it.

brief.thesis: Riven's entire kit is sub-275 range — Q (Broken Wings, 275), W (Ki Burst, 260), E (Valor, 250) — while Jayce's Cannon-stance Shock Blast reaches 600. The matchup is a question of whether Jayce respects that gap: lane advantage and solo-kill advantage both sit with Jayce (47.9% WR over 1034 games vs a 47.7% baseline), but the overall shape is even because one bad stance swap into her combo erases the lead instantly.

yourWindow.when: Her Q and E are both down
yourWindow.what: She has no dash and no damage-block left — this is when you step up and free-hit with autos and Q (To the Skies! / Shock Blast), or swap to Hammer stance and all-in with Q leap into E (Thundering Blow) knockback.

brief.thesis: This is a 52.5% K'Sante lane over 61 games because your CC is harder and more reliable than hers: Path Maker (W) is a guaranteed charge-then-stun on a 14→10s cooldown, while her only hard CC is Flawless Duet (E), a two-blade pincer on 16→10s cooldown that she must land cleanly on both sides to stun and Mark you. Outside of that window she only has a single-target dash (Bladesurge, Q) and a damage-reduction charge (Defiant Dance, W), neither of which locks you down. Overall shape is even because her Ionian Fervor attack-speed stacking and Vanguard's Edge (R) wall scale her into fights your early lane edge doesn't carry forward.

That's why the lane-advantage data favors Kled early while the head-to-head win rate (61%) favors K'Sante overall.

brief.thesis: Nasus's entire kit is built around uninterrupted Siphoning Strike (Q) last hits and Spirit Fire (E) zone control, and he has no dash or gap-closer to stop you from denying either. brief.thesis: This is classified EVEN with Kled holding solo-kill advantage, but the 37.5% head-to-head win rate over 48 games shows how badly it flips if you let the fight drag out. Kled's whole kit is built around short, violent windows — Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) yanks her out of position, W (Violent Tendencies) adds a 4-hit attack-speed burst, E (Jousting) lets you dash in and recast back through her. Illaoi's power instead comes from sustained skirmishes: Tentacle Smash procs, Harsh Lesson leaps, and Test of Spirit echoes that punish you for staying in extended exchanges, especially near impassible terrain where her passive tentacles spawn.

theirWindow.when: When E lands near wall-spawned tentacles
theirWindow.what: Test of Spirit (16/15/14/13/12s cooldown, 900 range) rips a spirit from you that echoes a percentage of damage dealt to it back onto you, and if it dies or you outrun it you become a Vessel that spawns more tentacles. Do not trade into the spirit — disengage with E (Jousting) and eat the Vessel timer passively rather than feeding the echo.

yourWindow.when: Levels 1-5, away from walls
yourWindow.what: Before her E rotation is smooth and before tentacles have accumulated on nearby terrain, Illaoi has no sustain crutch. Use Q's 800-range hook to yank her onto open ground, then chain E in and W's attack-speed burst to force a short trade she can't out-heal.

That asymmetry is why Malphite holds the measured 51% win rate and a solo-kill edge over 3,212 games despite Teemo controlling lane tempo early.

playing.title: Itemize armor for free E damage

brief.thesis: Volibear's whole kit is built to win extended trades: Q stuns and closes distance, W marks you and rewards a second cast with bonus damage and a heal, and his passive stacks Attack Speed off every action he takes. Malphite's E (Ground Slam) deals magic damage scaled off his own Armor and cuts enemy Attack Speed for a short duration, which directly blunts the on-hit chain Volibear needs to proc that heal. The matchup is even on paper (52% Malphite win rate over 1520 games) because whoever controls trade length wins — short pokes favor you, long ones favor him.

yourWindow.when: right after you land E (Ground Slam)

brief.thesis: Yorick trades in a straight line: Last Rites (4-6s cooldown) heals him through poke, Mourning Mist reaches from 700 range to shred your armor and slow you from outside your Q's 625 range, and Dark Procession lets him either wall you into the fight or wall himself out of it. Malphite's answer is the short burst his recharging Granite Shield passive allows plus armor-scaled Ground Slam, with no reliable follow-up before level 6 — and even then Unstoppable Force's 130-second base cooldown makes it a once-per-fight tool, not a lane staple. That structural mismatch in trade length is why Yorick holds the measured lane and solo-kill edge across 998 games, even with the champion win rate sitting close to even at 49.4%.

Measured win rate sits at an even 50% over 1,945 games, but Mordekaiser holds the lane and solo-kill edge — this is a matchup decided by who reads cooldowns better, not raw stats.

verdict.line: You win if you punish Sion's Q cooldown windows and shred his shield with empowered W before it pops; you lose if you trade passively and let his max-health stacking and level 6 Cannibalism carry the fight.

brief.thesis: Sion's whole early kit runs through two long-cooldown commitments — Q (Cryptic Gaze, 12-8s cooldown) and W (Death's Caress) — and Renekton's W (Ruthless Predator) directly answers both, stunning him out of the Q cast and, once empowered past 50 Fury, outright destroying the W shield before it detonates. That's why Renekton holds the lane and solo-kill edge here even though the raw head-to-head sits at 48.1% over 104 games — the tools favor you, the macro numbers are just close.

theirWindow.what: He gets a free auto-reset window and can toggle E to trade AD for health on top of it. Back off a step the instant the stun breaks rather than standing in follow-up autos.

yourWindow.when: Sion's Q is on cooldown or mid-charge
yourWindow.what: Walk him down and W him — at 0.75s base stun you lock him for a full extra auto, and if you're above 50 Fury the triple-slash version destroys his W shield outright and stuns for 1.5s. Follow with Q (Cull the Meek) since it hits everyone around you and heals you back.

brief.thesis: Renekton's entire edge is the pre-6 all-in: Teemo has no hard CC and only an 8-second Q (Blinding Dart) to stop a Fury-stacked W (Ruthless Predator) stun-chain. But once Teemo hits 6 and starts planting R (Noxious Trap) mushrooms, those poison-cloud zones plus stacking E (Toxic Shot) on-hit damage let him kite and siege from range, which is why the aggregate win rate (46.4%) sits below Renekton's overall baseline (49.6%) even though the lane and kill-pressure metrics favor him.

verdict.line: You lose if you eat free Corrosive Charge poke before level 3 and get Purged down before you can dash in; you win if you bank Fury past 50, dodge Q, and force the all-in before Urgot's items outscale your burst.

brief.thesis: Urgot has no reliable mobility beyond E (Disdain), a 475-range charge that only stuns if it connects — everything else is a ranged poke tool (Q, 800-range Corrosive Charge) or a stationary channel (W, Purge). Renekton's entire game plan is closing that gap: survive the poke window, use E (Slice and Dice) to dash in on cooldown, and convert once Fury crosses 50 so W (Ruthless Predator) upgrades from a 2-hit stun to a 3-hit shield-shredding stun. The data backs this as a genuinely even fight (48.1% over 1217 games) rather than a lane you're supposed to lose.

theirWindow.when: Levels 1-5, Q and W both up
theirWindow.what: Urgot can land Corrosive Charge at 800 range and follow with Purge's self-slowed auto channel without you being able to punish it. Hold position just outside Q range and farm with Q (Cull the Meek) instead of walking up for free autos.

yourWindow.when: Disdain (E) on cooldown, 14-16s
yourWindow.what: Once Urgot has used Disdain to clear a wave or whiffed it on you, he has no escape or hard CC for up to 16 seconds. Dash in with E, land W, and if Fury is above 50 the 3-hit empowered W stun-locks him for 1.5 seconds with no shield to peel it off.

brief.thesis: Irelia's Ionian Fervor passive stacks bonus attack speed off spell hits and caps with bonus on-hit damage, so she wins short trades the moment she lands two spells on you. Her E (Flawless Duet) stuns and Marks at range 850, and a Marked target refreshes her Q (Bladesurge) on a kill — so one connected E can chain straight into a kill combo before you can respond. Riven's own tools are reactive here: Valor (E) only blocks, Ki Burst (W) only stuns at point-blank range 260, and Blade of the Exile (R) isn't a real threat until mid-game. The 54.9% win rate over 731 games reflects Riven out-scaling a lane she does not win outright.

brief.thesis: Jayce's two stances give him both a ranged poke (Cannon-stance Shock Blast, range 600) and a melee leap/disengage kit (Hammer-stance To the Skies! and Thundering Blow), so he picks when the fight starts while you only have one short damage-block window per 10-6s on E (Valor) to answer it. Because his passive Hextech Capacitor grants move speed on every stance swap, he can poke, reposition, and still be ready to punish your dash the moment you commit. Your win condition is matching one E block to one poke, then closing the gap with Q (Broken Wings) and W (Ki Burst) before he resets range again.

Both champions are almost entirely cooldown-gated melee bruisers (no mana, short dash/stun timers), so this matchup is decided by who tracks the other's cooldowns, not by stats: 49.2% Sett win rate over 2,773 games is functionally a coin flip.

brief.thesis: Kled's mounted kit front-loads burst — Q (Bear Trap on a Rope) hooks and yanks from 800 range, then W (Violent Tendencies) and E (Jousting) stack on top — well beyond what Sett's 490-range E can answer in the first few trades. The 39.7% win rate over 116 games and Kled's measured solo-kill advantage both come from this gap; Sett closes it by grinding Skaarl's health down in extended fights, since a dismounted Kled loses his hook and deals less damage to champions.

theirWindow.what: He can hook you from 800 range, yank you in, then Joust (dash, 550 range, re-castable to dash back) through you while Violent Tendencies' attack-speed burst is live. Don't stand in his Q arc at the wave's edge during this window — let minions eat the hook.

yourWindow.when: Kled dismounted after Skaarl's HP breaks
yourWindow.what: His Q becomes Pocket Pistol — a knockback with no hook or yank — and his champion damage drops. This is when you commit: stack your passive's missing-health regen, cash in W (Haymaker)'s stored Grit for the shield and true-damage burst, and look for E (Facebreaker) if you can line him up against minions or terrain.

playing.title: Lead extended trades with Q
playing.detail: Knuckle Down's bonus damage scales off his max health, so it stays relevant even as he stacks resistances — throw it in every fight that goes past the first exchange.

playing.title: Use R to deny his setup

brief.thesis: Urgot is a ranged duelist whose Q (Corrosive Charge, 800 range, 10s-8s cooldown) and Echoing Flames chip Sett down before he can ever close the gap, which is why this matchup sits at only 44.7% over 141 games despite Sett's raw all-in power. Sett has no dash, so every approach while Urgot's Q and Purge are both up gets punished, while every approach after he dumps them is a free all-in. Sett's E (Facebreaker) only stuns if there's a minion on the opposite side of Urgot from him — without that, it just slows — so wave position decides whether an all-in kills him or turns into a losing stand-and-fire contest.

brief.thesis: Camille's entire burst case runs through one mechanic: Precision Protocol (Q) can be held and recast for drastically more damage, and that recast is a single-target hit Shen can simply block. OP.GG's own read on this matchup is literally to save Feint (W) for that recast — do that consistently and her all-in stops being an all-in. Everything else (Hookshot engages, the ultimate anchor) only matters if that one trade goes through.

yourWindow.what: Hold W and watch her first Q cast. The moment she re-presses it for the big delayed hit, pop Feint (9/8/7/6/5s CD) to absorb it outright, then punish with Vorpal Blade while her Q is on full cooldown.

Shen's answer isn't to out-duel that — it's to play Vorpal Blade pokes at safe range, deny his E (Apprehend) hook windows with Feint, and treat the lane as a stall until Stand United lets you win the game from somewhere else on the map.

brief.thesis: Gangplank's Parrrley (625 range) outranges your Vorpal Blade (475 range), so he poke-farms you for free while you have no answer except absorbing it. His W, Remove Scurvy, clears your only hard CC and heals him back, so Shadow Dash all-ins only work on a timer. Your real edge isn't the 1v1 — it's that Stand United lets you abandon a losing lane state and swing fights elsewhere, which is why Shen holds a 51.4% win rate overall even though this specific matchup sits at 48.7% across 1,773 games.

verdict.line: You lose extended trades before level 6 while Gnar pokes freely at range 1100; you win once Titanic Hydra is online and he has to respect your taunt.

brief.thesis: Gnar's mini-form Q (Boomerang Throw, range 1100) outranges Shen's Q (Vorpal Blade, range 475) by over double, and his E (Hop, 475 range) resets the trade by bouncing away before Shen's Shadow Dash (575 range, 16s cooldown at rank 1) can land. The 48.8% head-to-head over 1431 games and Gnar's lane/solo-kill edge both come from that early range and mobility mismatch, not from Shen being outclassed once items come online.

yourWindow.what: Shadow Dash in to taunt. He can't disengage without E, so this is your one reliable window to land Q (Vorpal Blade) repeatedly and life-tap back the damage he dealt poking you.

verdict.line: You lose if you keep getting caught by her E's spirit tether near her Tentacle walls; you win if you survive to Thornmail and start swinging side lanes with your ultimate instead of forcing lane.

brief.thesis: Illaoi's kit revolves entirely around E (Test of Spirit): once the spirit lands on Shen, she follows with W and Q while nearby Tentacles also swing at him, and if he doesn't break the tether fast enough he becomes a Vessel feeding Tentacles that heal her on every champion hit. Shen has no ability that repositions him away from that — W is a self-shield, E is a taunting engage dash — so he can't out-footwork it. That's exactly why the measured data has Illaoi holding both the lane and solo-kill edge (49.3% for Shen here versus his 51.3% baseline), and why the standard advice is to disengage immediately rather than commit.

theirWindow.what: She'll follow with W (Harsh Lesson) and Q (Tentacle Smash) while the spirit echoes damage back onto you. Walk far enough away or kill the spirit immediately, or you become a Vessel feeding her tentacle-heal passive.

yourWindow.when: Her E and R are both on cooldown
yourWindow.what: Step up and throw Q (Vorpal Blade) for free poke and the life-tap heal — with no spirit tether or tentacle smash available, she can't punish you for standing in range.

verdict.line: You lose extended 1v1 trades and solo-kill exchanges level 1-5 when Irelia lands her full combo, but Shen still wins the matchup 54% of the time over 1,049 games by refusing those trades and using his global ultimate to swing fights elsewhere.

brief.thesis: Irelia's Q (Bladesurge) dash-strike plus stacking Ionian Fervor attack speed means any extended stand-and-trade favors her, which is why OP.GG marks both lane and solo-kill advantage in her favor. Shen's kit isn't built to win that duel — W (Feint) exists to eat her all-in rather than to out-damage her, and Q (Vorpal Blade) is a sustain tool, not a poke win condition. The 54% head-to-head comes from refusing her preferred fight and converting Shen's global-range R (Stand United) into pressure on the rest of the map instead.

theirWindow.when: Irelia at full passive stacks
theirWindow.what: At max Ionian Fervor stacks she gains bonus on-hit damage on top of the attack speed, so she wins any stand-and-trade outright. Disengage, let minions eat her autos, and don't contest with Q (Vorpal Blade) until the stacks decay.

yourWindow.when: After she throws or wastes E (Flawless Duet)
yourWindow.what: Flawless Duet is her only hard CC and sits on a 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s cooldown. Once it's been thrown into minions or missed, she has no stun to punish your approach — this is when to land E (Shadow Dash) and follow with Q (Vorpal Blade) for a safe poke.

Jax's E starts at an 18-second cooldown and only drops to 10s at max rank, while Shen's E (Shadow Dash) starts at 16s and drops to 8s, meaning Shen gets more taunt windows per minute than Jax gets stun windows by the mid-game.

brief.thesis: Jayce's Cannon-stance Shock Blast (Q) fired through his own Acceleration Gate (E) gains extended missile speed, range, and damage, while Shen's entire engage kit — Feint (W), Shadow Dash (E, range 575), Vorpal Blade (Q, range 475) — only functions once he closes to melee range. This lane is won by surviving his poke windows and using Shadow Dash to punish his stance-swap rhythm, not by out-trading him at range.

verdict.line: You lose if you let Camille land Hookshot's knockup with Precision Protocol already active and no Blinding Dart up; you win if you poke with Toxic Shot from range and blind every engage she commits to.

brief.thesis: Camille's entire kill combo is Hookshot (E) knocking you up into a guaranteed Precision Protocol (Q) empowered auto — that guarantee is the whole threat, not raw damage. Teemo's Blinding Dart makes that follow-up attack miss even while you're in the knockup, so the trade pattern is: harass with Toxic Shot poison from outside 325 range, then blind the exact instant she commits E or recasts Q. That single interaction is why this sits at 53.2% over 1167 games rather than genuinely losing.

yourWindow.when: the moment she commits E or activates Q
yourWindow.what: Land Blinding Dart immediately so her empowered attack whiffs outright, wasting both the cooldown and the bonus damage; she's now stuck at melee range with nothing to punish you for walking away.

brief.thesis: Cho'Gath's Rupture (Q) reaches 950 range at level 1, out-ranging Teemo's 680-range Blinding Dart and his autoattacks, so Cho can poke and zone Teemo safely for free early. But Teemo never needs to approach to trade — Toxic Shot (E) procs on every autoattack with no cooldown, so he out-damages Cho over a long trade as long as he refuses to walk into Rupture range to start it. That's exactly why the head-to-head sits at 50.7% over 152 games: the lane rewards the Teemo who waits, not the one who engages first.

brief.thesis: Jayce is two champions stapled together: Cannon stance is a 600-range poke bot with Shock Blast (Q), Hammer stance is a dash-knockback brawler with To the Skies! (Q) into Thundering Blow (E). Every trade in this lane is decided by which stance he's in when he commits, and Teemo's entire plan is to punish the Hammer-stance engage with Blinding Dart (Q) while refusing to stand in Cannon-stance poke range. Early levels favor his longer effective threat range and solo-kill setups; once you hit your item spikes, stacked Toxic Shot (E) and Liandry's burn out-damage his bruiser build in extended fights.

Hold Blinding Dart (Q) until he commits the dash — landing it blinds the follow-up autos and lets you walk out before E's knockback resets the exchange in his favor.

yourWindow.when: his Hammer-stance Q is on visible cooldown
yourWindow.what: With To the Skies! down he has no gap closer for up to 16 seconds early, only Cannon-stance poke. Walk up, stack Toxic Shot (E) autos, and shove the wave — he can't punish you for holding lane presence until that cooldown resets.

brief.thesis: Volibear's Q (Thundering Smash) only stuns 'the first one he Attacks,' which means he has to already be in range to use it — and Gwen's W (Hallowed Mist) exists specifically to deny that target-lock by making her untargetable to anyone standing outside the mist. The whole lane is about timing your all-in to when that mist is down, because Gwen has no real ranged disengage otherwise: her Q is a 450-range cone, not a dash, and her only mobility tool (E) needs to land a hit to refund its cooldown. The data backs this up — Volibear holds both the lane-win and solo-kill edge here, so patience, not greed, is what converts that edge.

yourWindow.what: She has zero targeting-denial left. Walk to 325 range, open W (Frenzied Maul) to mark her, follow with Q (Thundering Smash) to stun, then recast W on the same mark for the bonus damage and heal.
